en: Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the ground, which prevents you from slipping on wet school floors.
Never touch plugged-in appliances with wet hands because water conducts electricity and can cause a severe, dangerous shock.
Wrapping yourself in a wool blanket keeps you warm by trapping your body heat and preventing it from escaping.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can permanently damage your eyes and cause blindness.
Listening to loud music through earphones for too long can permanently damage the tiny hair cells in your inner ear.
Pushing a heavy box up a wooden ramp uses an inclined plane, making it safer and easier than lifting it straight up.
Keep strong neodymium magnets away from pacemakers and phones because their powerful magnetic fields can disrupt normal electronic functions.
Always carry heavy backpacks using both shoulder straps to distribute the gravitational pull evenly and prevent painful spine injuries.
Eating carbohydrate-rich foods provides chemical energy that your cells convert into kinetic energy, giving you power to run and play.
During a thunderstorm, stay inside because a building's metal lightning rod safely conducts lightning's electrical energy directly into the ground.
Using a wheelbarrow acts as a second-class lever, allowing you to safely transport heavy garden soil with much less effort.
Wearing reflective tape at night makes you visible because the material reflects car headlights directly back to the driver.
